title: The False Allure of "Security by Obscurity": A Game-Theoretic Approach
abstract: arXiv:2610.12858v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: "Security by obscurity," or the idea that hiding how a system works helps protect it from adversaries, has long been poorly regarded in the security community. Yet its intuitive appeal persists, and it has resurfaced repeatedly in industry practices and public debates over the years. The logic, on the one hand, is that open scrutiny of systems is the best way to find and respond to problems; and on the other hand, that too much openness can increase risk by giving adversaries a roadmap for attack. This isn't purely a technical question, but a human one: it's about how attackers and good-faith security researchers respond to openness in the real world. As such, security experts base their stance on decades of community experience; however, the field lacks empirical or theoretical foundations to back up these long-standing beliefs. translated_title: “模糊安全”的虚假魅力：一种博弈论方法
translated_abstract: “模糊安全”（security by obscurity），即通过隐藏系统的工作原理来保护系统免受对手攻击的理念，长期以来在安全界备受诟病。然而，其直觉上的吸引力依然存在，并在多年来的行业实践和公众辩论中反复出现。一方面，其逻辑是：对系统的公开审查是发现和应对问题的最佳方式；另一方面，过度的开放可能为对手提供攻击路线图，从而增加风险。这并非纯粹的技术问题，而是一个关于人的问题：它关乎攻击者和善意的安全研究人员在现实世界中如何应对系统的开放性。正因如此，安全专家的立场建立在数十年的社区经验之上；然而，该领域一直缺乏支撑这些长期信念的实证或理论基础。我们首次对“模糊安全”进行了严格的建模，旨在刻画理性主体将如何（应对系统的开放性）……
tldr: 本文首次运用博弈论方法对“模糊安全”理念进行严格建模，为安全界长期依赖经验直觉的“开放还是隐匿”之争提供了理论分析基础。
en_tdlr: This paper provides the first rigorous game-theoretic modeling of "security by obscurity," establishing a theoretical foundation for the security community's long-standing, experience-based debate between openness and concealment.
